regulations.area: Fort Bragg to Point Arena · California · Mendocino Groundfish Management Area
regulations.scope: Reviewed 2026 recreational boat species rules for the Fort Bragg–Point Arena and Shelter Cove–Fort Bragg outer-coast planning extents. Exact current MPA boundaries, in-season notices, route and launch clearance remain separate.
common_notes: The Mendocino Management Area runs from 40°10′ N near Cape Mendocino to 38°57.5′ N at Point Arena. Rules in Northern and San Francisco areas differ.
The 2026 Fort Bragg ocean salmon season is closed for the remainder of the year. Do not apply the fall opening south of 38°02′ N here.

MPAs, current in-season actions, health and gear declarations, exact fishing method and possession of other species can restrict an otherwise open season. A season card does not clear a route or harbor entrance.

rules-gear.name: CDFW finfish gear and general rules
rules-gear.review_note: Reviewed 2026 CDFW general finfish gear text: lingcod and rockfish aboard impose one-line/two-hook limits; salmon gear is separately restricted.

rules-invertebrates.name: CDFW invertebrate gear rules
rules-invertebrates.review_note: Reviewed current CDFW section 29.80 gear text for recreational crab traps, hoop nets, snares, marking and tending; gear permission is separate from season status.

rules-whales.name: CDFW whale-safe crab restrictions
rules-whales.review_note: Reviewed CDFW 2026–27 whale-safe status: recreational Dungeness season is presently closed, and November trap authorization needs the later zone declaration.

rules-health.name: CDFW fishery health closures
rules-health.review_note: Reviewed CDFW fishery-health notices and Mendocino-related advisories; no health page was treated as an automatic future crab or finfish clearance.

rules-ocean.name: CDFW official regulation index
rules-ocean.review_note: Reviewed the 2026 CDFW ocean index and links to species, in-season and health rules; the index alone grants no location-specific permission.

rules-groundfish.name: CDFW groundfish
rules-groundfish.review_note: Reviewed June 2026 CDFW groundfish summary: Mendocino boat season Apr–Dec all depths, RCG ten with two vermilion/sunset here, lingcod two at 22 inches and descending device.

rules-inseason.name: CDFW in-season changes
rules-inseason.review_note: Reviewed dated CDFW in-season actions through September 11, including the Fort Bragg August salmon closure and Fishing Zone 3 recreational trap restriction; future openings need new review.

rules-salmon.name: CDFW salmon
rules-salmon.review_note: Reviewed CDFW 2026 salmon page: the September fall season starts south of 38°02′ N, not in the Fort Bragg Management Area; north-of-Point-Conception barbless gear rules remain relevant.

rules-crab.name: CDFW crab
rules-crab.review_note: Reviewed CDFW permanent redirect to the canonical crab page and its September 24 recreational regulations and FAQ. The normalized content hash matches the previously reviewed source; current season, gear, whale and health checks remain separate.

rules-book.name: CDFW 2026 ocean sport fishing booklet
rules-book.review_note: Reviewed original 2026 CDFW ocean booklet: California halibut two fish north of Point Sur, albacore 25 north of Point Conception, crab limits and gear, and the §27.65 fillet rule limited to south of Point Arena.

rules-proposals.name: California FGC rulemaking: effective and pending changes
rules-proposals.review_note: Reviewed 2026 Fish and Game Commission rulemaking index: groundfish conformance is proposed without an operative effective date in this packet and was not treated as current law.

rules-tuna-federal.name: Federal recreational Pacific tuna rules · 50 CFR 660.721
rules-tuna-federal.review_note: Reviewed original current eCFR 50 CFR 660.721 section: 25 albacore north of Point Conception, ten if a trip enters the southern EEZ, and trip/day possession constraints.

rules-salmon-pdf.name: CDFW 2026 ocean salmon season flyer · August update
rules-salmon-pdf.review_note: Reviewed original August 19 CDFW salmon flyer: Fort Bragg August 10–31 closure, no fall season north of 38°02′ N, and salmon rod/hook restrictions.

rules-groundfish-pdf.name: CDFW Mendocino groundfish season table
rules-groundfish-pdf.review_note: Reviewed original 2026 Mendocino groundfish PDF: Apr–Dec all-depth boat season, ten RCG with one copper/two canary/two vermilion-sunset, two lingcod at 22 inches, no-retention species and descending device.

rules-pacific-halibut.name: CDFW Pacific halibut season and quota
rules-pacific-halibut.review_note: Reviewed current CDFW Pacific halibut page: north of Point Arena open Apr 1–Nov 15 or quota closure, one fish with no minimum size and one-line/two-hook angling rule.

rules-mendocino.name: CDFW Mendocino management area rules
rules-mendocino.review_note: Reviewed CDFW Mendocino regional page updated August 10: Fort Bragg salmon closed rest of 2026, Dungeness closed with scheduled Nov 7 opener, California and Pacific halibut distinct, and local bounds.

mpa-russian-gulch.name: CDFW Russian Gulch SMCA
mpa-russian-gulch.review_note: Reviewed CDFW Russian Gulch SMCA page: recreational take is allowed under current rules, though SkipperCast conservatively excludes the MPA from target geometry and exports.

mpa-point-arena.name: CDFW Point Arena and Sea Lion Cove MPAs
mpa-point-arena.review_note: Reviewed CDFW Point Arena and Sea Lion Cove MPA page: SMR no take, Point Arena SMCA salmon trolling only, Sea Lion Cove SMCA finfish exception; app still excludes all mapped MPA targets.

mpa-big-flat.name: CDFW Big Flat SMCA
mpa-big-flat.review_note: Inspected CDFW Big Flat SMCA text and coordinates: ordinary recreational take is prohibited except salmon trolling and Dungeness by trap, hoop net or hand; tribal exemptions are separately listed. The app conservatively excludes all mapped MPA areas from targets and exports.

mpa-ten-mile.name: CDFW Ten Mile SMR and SMCAs
mpa-ten-mile.review_note: Inspected CDFW Ten Mile SMR, Ten Mile Beach SMCA and Ten Mile Estuary SMCA text and coordinates: SMR no take, Beach recreational Dungeness by trap/hoop net/hand, Estuary waterfowl only; listed tribal exemptions are separate. The app excludes all three mapped areas from targets and exports.

mpa-double-cone.name: CDFW Double Cone Rock SMCA
mpa-double-cone.review_note: Inspected CDFW Double Cone Rock SMCA regulations and published coordinates. Ordinary recreational take is limited to salmon by trolling and Dungeness by trap, hoop net or hand, with separate tribal exemptions. App target/export geometry excludes the whole mapped SMCA.

closure-vizcaino-rock.name: CDFW Vizcaino Rock seasonal special closure
closure-vizcaino-rock.review_note: Inspected CDFW Vizcaino Rock special-closure text and coordinates. Entry is barred March 1 through August 31 within the specified 300 ft shoreline buffer, except listed official duties or CDFW permission. The app conservatively excludes this mapped closure year-round from targets and exports.

mpa-mackerricher.name: CDFW MacKerricher SMCA
mpa-mackerricher.review_note: Inspected CDFW MacKerricher SMCA regulations and published coordinates. Commercial and recreational take follows current general rules, with a commercial kelp prohibition. App target/export geometry excludes this mapped SMCA despite the recreational exception.

lingcod.name: Lingcod
lingcod.season: Apr 1–Dec 31, 2026 · boat fishing at all depths in the Mendocino Management Area.
lingcod.bag: 2 per person daily; 2 in possession. Separate from the 10-fish RCG limit.
details: Use one line with no more than two hooks when targeting lingcod, or when lingcod are aboard. Your double-drop rig fits that limit.
Carry a descending device ready for immediate use.
Fillets aboard: at least 14 in, with all skin attached.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

rockfish.name: Rockfish / rock cod
rockfish.season: Apr 1–Dec 31, 2026 · boat fishing at all depths in the Mendocino Management Area.
rockfish.bag: 10 total rockfish, cabezon and greenlings combined per person daily and in possession.
rockfish.size: No minimum length for retained rockfish. Species must be identified.
details: Within the 10: at most 1 copper, 2 canary, and 2 vermilion/sunset rockfish combined.
No retention of yelloweye, quillback, cowcod or bronzespotted rockfish.
Use one line with no more than two hooks when targeting rockfish, or when rockfish are aboard. Carry a descending device ready for use.
Retained rockfish fillets must have all skin attached.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

halibut.name: California halibut
halibut.season: California halibut: year-round in the reviewed 2026 Mendocino rules; distinct from Pacific halibut.
halibut.bag: 2 per person daily and in possession north of Point Sur.
details: California halibut only; Pacific halibut has a separate quota, season and one-fish limit.
General ocean hook-and-line rules apply. With rockfish or lingcod aboard, use one line and no more than two hooks; salmon aboard triggers salmon gear rules.

Do not gaff an undersized fish. Check current vessel-filleting and species-identification rules before filleting aboard; the special 16¾-inch California halibut fillet rule in §27.65(b)(6) is written for fish taken or possessed south of Point Arena.
Keep the fish whole when in doubt about size, identification or the rules at a boundary.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

salmon.name: Chinook salmon
salmon.season: Ocean salmon is closed in the Fort Bragg Management Area for the remainder of 2026.
salmon.bag: No retention while the Fort Bragg recreational ocean salmon season is closed.
salmon.size: Not applicable during the 2026 closed season.
details: CDFW says the Fort Bragg Management Area is closed for the remainder of 2026; the September fall opener begins south of 38°02′ N and does not apply here.
Future openings depend on new federal and state action and require a fresh review. Do not troll for salmon in closed waters.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

albacore.name: Albacore tuna
albacore.season: Year-round in reviewed 2026 state and federal rules, subject to current notices in U.S. waters north of Point Conception.
albacore.bag: 25 per person daily and in possession, in addition to the general 20-finfish limit.
albacore.size: No minimum size in these recreational rules.
details: The albacore limit drops to 10 south of Point Conception (34°27′ N). This card does not cover Mexico.
General ocean hook-and-line rules apply; fish already aboard can impose stricter rod and hook limits.
If processing tuna aboard south of Point Conception, follow the tuna-specific fillet, skin and bag-label requirements in §27.65. This card covers day trips; multi-day possession rules differ.
If any part of an albacore trip enters U.S. EEZ waters south of 34°27′ N, no more than 10 albacore per person may be onboard for that trip; the rule is not determined only by where a fish was caught.
Federal tuna limits apply per 24-hour period at sea and never authorize more than one daily bag per calendar day. Multi-day possession needs separate review.

South of Point Conception (34°27′ N), tuna processed aboard must use the six-piece arrangement required by §27.65, keep all skin attached, and be individually bagged with its species labeled. That specific six-piece rule does not apply to processing north of the line.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

dungeness.name: Dungeness crab
dungeness.season: Closed after Jul 31, 2026. Nov 7, 2026 is a scheduled reopening, subject to health and gear declarations.
dungeness.bag: When open: 10 per person daily; 10 in possession on a private boat.
dungeness.size: 5¾ in shell width, measured across the body just in front of the side spines, excluding those spines. Carry a crab gauge.
details: Season opening and trap permission are separate. Mendocino November trap clearance has not been confirmed; check the current CDFW whale-safe and health notices for the precise fishing zone.
A crab-trap validation is required to use traps. Maximum 10 deployed traps per person; required escape rings, destruct device, GO ID and buoy markings apply.
Hoop nets and snares have separate gear rules. A trap restriction does not itself close those methods, but the season and health closures still apply.
Check the current 2026 hoop-net marking rules and all gear details in §29.80 before setting gear.
Crab traps may not be deployed during the seven days before the Dungeness season opens. Service deployed traps at intervals no greater than nine days, weather conditions permitting (§29.80(c)).
Crab loop traps or snares may have no more than six loops. Hoop nets must be raised and inspected at least every two hours (§29.80).

North of Point Arguello, each hoop net must have the required surface buoy marked with the operator’s GO ID; the main buoy may not exceed 6 in in diameter or 14 in in length. An optional orange marker marked H and its connecting line have additional marking specifications; check §29.80(b) before rigging.

trap.note: Trap permission is checked separately from the Dungeness season and health closures. Confirm the current recreational trap declaration, validation, marking and tending rules before setting.

hoop.note: A hoop net is a different gear category from a crab trap. Follow the current hoop-net construction, attendance and deployment rules; season and health closures still apply.

snare.note: Use the current snare definition and gear limits. A trap restriction does not by itself establish permission to take Dungeness; the season and health checks also apply.

pacific-halibut.name: Pacific halibut
pacific-halibut.season: Apr 1–Nov 15, 2026 north of Point Arena, or until the quota is reached earlier; this Mendocino card ends at Point Arena.
details: When angling, use no more than one line with two hooks attached.
Quota can close the season early; check the current CDFW halibut page and hotline before fishing.
Pacific halibut is distinct from California halibut; do not apply the two-fish California halibut limit.
Check the exact MPA, method and all other gear rules at the selected position and date.

rod.note: This profile covers recreational boat angling. One line with a maximum of two hooks; quota and geographic notices still apply.

area_notices.name: Mendocino coast marine protected areas
area_notices.note: Point Arena SMR prohibits take; Point Arena SMCA allows salmon trolling only; Sea Lion Cove SMCA allows finfish but not crab take. Russian Gulch SMCA allows recreational take under current rules. SkipperCast conservatively excludes all mapped MPA fishing targets until exact legal boundaries and method exceptions are reviewed at the selected position.

area_notices.name: North Mendocino protected areas and seasonal closure
area_notices.note: Big Flat and Double Cone Rock SMCAs allow specified salmon trolling and Dungeness methods for non-tribal recreational take. Ten Mile SMR has no take; Ten Mile Beach SMCA permits Dungeness by trap, hoop net or hand, and Ten Mile Estuary SMCA permits only waterfowl take. MacKerricher SMCA allows recreational take under current rules. Vizcaino Rock has a March 1–August 31 no-entry special closure. These rules do not override current seasons, tribal provisions or the app’s conservative exclusion of mapped MPAs from fishing targets and exports.

limitations: Landing port is not a catch position; named grounds are broad reports, not GPS fixes.
Reports are a selected sample, with unknown effort and missing unsuccessful trips.
Satellite temperature and HF radar measure surface context, not bottom conditions.
Daily observations are not a seven-day bite forecast or live entrance clearance.
